transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees (recorded): Ethan Park, Priya Nair (Redwood); Jordan Blake, Aisha Khan, Marta Ivanova, Tom Reyes, Liam Ortiz (Aurora)

Summary:
Quick procurement review: finalize MSA and DPA redlines, confirm SLA targets (99.9 vs 99.95), discuss pricing approval for dedicated capacity pilot, confirm security artifacts (SOC2, ISO, KMS), and plan onboarding steps. Next steps and owners noted.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and SLA credits
- DPA & data residency / retention
- Security artifacts: SOC2, ISO27001, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML/SCIM
- Pricing: committed reserved capacity vs hosted overage rates and approval process
- Onboarding timeline and pilot scope

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Can you hear me all right?
[00:05] Jordan (Aurora): Yep loud and clear, thanks Ethan.
[00:08] Ethan: Great. So agenda for today's call is procurement/legal review — MSA, DPA, SLAs, pricing approvals and next steps for vendor onboarding. I think we have Priya from our SE team to walk through the technical assurances.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood): Hi all. I'll kick off with a quick summary of the security artifacts we can share, then hand off to Ethan for commercial.
[00:27] Marta (Aurora): Perfect, we're particularly interested in key management and audit logs — plus any on-prem/VPC details.
[00:33] Priya: Totally. We have SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 attestation, architecture diagram showing dedicated VPC options, and KMS integration details. On the private deployment side we can offer a VPC-private control plane or an on-prem appliance for air-gapped needs — language is in the security pack.
[00:50] Aisha (Aurora Legal): Will that include encryption key lifecycle details? Our legal needs KMS responsibilities spelled out in the DPA.
[00:55] Priya: Yes, we include KMS options — customer-managed keys with HSM support and details on key rotation. The doc includes the responsibilities matrix, though Aisha you may want to redline the DPA for language about key custody.
[01:05] Aisha: Good, we'll look for that.
[01:08] Ethan: On the MSA side, we sent an initial redline last week; we've seen some notes from your team. I wanted to go through the main sticky points: SLA uptime target and credits, indemnity carve-outs, and data residency obligations.
[01:22] Tom (Aurora): On SLAs — our ops team is pushing for P99 latency SLO for inference and a 99.95% availability SLA for hosted endpoints. I know historically Redwood has a 99.9% guarantee for hosted; what's the delta and what would additional credits look like?
[01:36] Priya: Quick callout: we surface P95/P99 latency numbers in the console but SLA is availability-based. We can look at 99.95 for a dedicated reserved capacity contract depending on commit level; typically that level needs reserved/dedicated nodes and operational commitments. Credits scale with the percentage. I can pull the exact credit schedule.
[01:50] Jordan: What kind of financial credit are we talking about? Our procurement needs a table to show to finance.
[01:54] Ethan: We usually do a prorated service credit: at 99.9% it's X% of the monthly invoice, at 99.95% it's slightly less frequent incidents but we can negotiate. I'll send the official SLA table.
[02:06] Marta: Also want to confirm automatic fallback behavior. If dedicated capacity is saturated do you failover to hosted endpoints? We need to understand data paths and whether any data leaves our region.
[02:18] Priya: Smart routing can fail over to another capacity tier but only to region-compatible clusters; we honor customer data residency controls — no data is routed outside approved regions without consent. For dedicated pools we provide isolation and can disallow cross-tenant fallback. Those details are in the deployment architecture doc.
[02:36] Aisha: About DPA — we have a few standard asks: subcontractor list, data processing purposes, deletion windows, and breach notification timelines. Can Redwood commit to 30 day notification for incidents?
[02:48] Ethan: Our standard is 72 hours for security incidents; 30 days is typically for longer notifications like regulatory inquiries. We can commit to 72 hours for security incidents and include a clause for regulatory notice timelines — happy to look at your redline.
[03:02] Aisha: 72 hours is fine, we just need it written in the DPA.
[03:05] Jordan: Pricing — high level, we're evaluating a 3 month dedicated pilot with a view to an annual reserved commit. Can you confirm pilot pricing and how approvals route internally? We need a price sheet to circulate.
[03:18] Ethan: Yes — we can quote a pilot rate for a small dedicated pool, and include a convert-to-reserved discount if you commit within 60 days of pilot end. I'll attach a consolidated pricing sheet with tiered discounts.
[03:30] Liam (Aurora Sourcing): Who signs the invoices for pilots? We need the procurement flow to match our PO system.
[03:34] Ethan: We'll accept standard PO terms and can invoice monthly; for reserved we typically do a monthly/quarterly billing schedule aligned to the commit. Finance details go in the SOW.
[03:45] Tom: Is there any vendor lock-in? We want to make sure we can export KV cache or model assets if we choose to move to self-hosting later.
[03:54] Priya: Models and checkpoints depend on licensing; open model variants are available to download per their licenses. Cache data is ephemeral; we can provide export utilities for customer data like prompts and logs. We'll clarify export procedures.
[04:05] Jordan: On the DPA clause about subprocessors, can we get a list and an approval flow?
[04:11] Ethan: Yes — we'll provide current subprocessor list and a process for notification/approval for material changes.
[04:16] Marta: Security controls — do you support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning? We need role sync and RBAC mapping into our IdP.
[04:25] Priya: Yes, SAML SSO is supported, SCIM for provisioning, and we support SSO with OIDC in some cases. We'll send the SSO integration guide.
[04:32] Aisha: A couple legal points we flagged: indemnity caps and limitation of liability — looks like your standard has aggregate cap equal to the fees paid in last 12 months. We typically ask for a higher cap for security breaches.
[04:44] Ethan: We can discuss an increased cap for GDPR-level security incidents — that's a negotiation point; we'll mark it for legal.
[04:50] Aisha: Good.
[04:52] Jordan: For procurement approvals I need a one-pager summarizing the commercial ask, pilot duration, pricing, and SLA options to present next week. Can you do that?
[04:59] Ethan: Absolutely — I'll prepare a one-pager and pricing summary.
[05:03] Priya: I'll include the tech appendix with architecture diagrams and a short runbook for the pilot.
[05:09] Marta: Regarding monitoring — what telemetry do you expose? We need per-request logs, latency histograms, and token-level cost breakdown for chargebacks.
[05:19] Priya: Console exposes per-route token costs, latency percentiles, traces linked to request ids. We also offer log export to GCS/S3 and can stream to Splunk/Datadog.
[05:30] Liam: About SLAs again — how are credits calculated? Is there an automatic credit or do we need to claim?
[05:36] Ethan: Credits are applied after validation; customer files a claim and we run an automated check of uptime metrics; in many cases credits are granted automatically if metrics indicate an outage. We'll include the credit claim flow in the SLA appendix.
[05:50] Aisha: Any regulatory certifications for healthcare? We are evaluating a future PHI workload.
[05:56] Priya: We don't sign BAAs for hosted multi-tenant at this time; for PHI use cases we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with additional contract terms — we can discuss a private control plane or on-prem option to meet BAA requirements.
[06:12] Tom: For the pilot, can we scope a small PHI-safe subset to test redaction and logging in a private env?
[06:20] Priya: Yes, we can create a private pilot environment and run limited PHI-safe tests with agreed safeguards. That would likely require a Private onboarding addendum.
[06:32] Jordan: What's the typical legal turnaround time you've seen? Our compliance calendar is tight.
[06:37] Ethan: For standard customers it's 2-4 weeks after we exchange initial redlines; for enterprise with significant custom language, 4-8 weeks. Given your timeline we can prioritize.
[06:48] Aisha: We'll aim to get initial DPA redlines back by next week.
[06:53] Ethan: Great.
[06:55] Priya: A quick question on operational readiness — will your team run benchmarks (latency/cost) as part of the pilot? We recommend a short benchmark run to size the dedicated pool.
[07:06] Tom: Yes, we want to run our typical inference workload and compare P95/P99 across dedicated vs hosted.
[07:12] Priya: Perfect — we'll provide a benchmark harness and sample configs.
[07:17] Jordan: On onboarding, do you provide an implementation manager or is it a self-service kickoff? We have limited SRE bandwidth.
[07:24] Ethan: For pilots we include onboarding support hours with an assigned solutions engineer (Priya) and optional professional services for a fee. We'll outline included hours.
[07:33] Marta: Data retention — what are default log retention windows? We need 1 year for audit logs.
[07:40] Priya: Default is 90 days but we can extend to 1 year as an add-on or for enterprise plans; we'll include retention options in the security pack.
[07:50] Liam: Slightly random — how do you handle egress costs when using dedicated capacity in our cloud region?
[07:57] Ethan: Egress depends on deployment topology; if you use our hosted endpoints in your region egress is standard cloud egress; for private deployments you control egress since it's in your VPC. We'll call out egress patterns in the SOW.
[08:08] Aisha: Back to DPA, we have a clause about ephemeral cache — we need assurance that inference prompts are not used to train models.
[08:16] Ethan: We have a no-training clause for customer data — we can add an explicit statement that customer prompts & responses are excluded from model training and are only used for debugging with consent. We'll put that in the DPA.
[08:29] Jordan: Anything else on pricing — do you offer net-30 invoices?
[08:33] Ethan: Yes, net-30 is standard; we can accommodate PO-based billing.
[08:37] Tom: Pilot scope reminder — small dedicated pool, 4-weeks, run benchmarks and a short PHI-safe test if we sign an addendum.
[08:46] Priya: Noted. We'll deliver benchmark harness, runbook, and pilot SOW draft.
[08:52] Jordan: On governance — can we include a quarterly security review clause in the MSA?
[08:58] Ethan: We can include an annual or quarterly review clause as part of the enterprise SOW. We'll propose quarterly for the pilot-to-contract transition.
[09:07] Aisha: Any other outstanding redlines from Redwood's side?
[09:10] Ethan: We'll clean up indemnity language to propose a middle ground and include the SLA credit schedule. Expect a redlined MSA from us by Thursday (2026-07-22).
[09:20] Marta: We'll review and circulate DPA redlines by 2026-07-21.
[09:24] Jordan: OK, to recap next steps. Ethan to send MSA redline and pricing one-pager; Priya to send security pack and bench harness; Aurora to return DPA redlines and confirm budget. Then schedule pilot kickoff once MSA is agreed.
[09:40] Ethan: Exactly. Thanks all — we'll follow up in email and attach the artifacts.
[09:44] Tom: Thanks everyone.
[09:46] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: auto transcription had a few mis-hearings of product names (e.g., "Red wood" vs Redwood) and occasional speaker label swaps; timestamps are approximate.
